title.purpose: the piece's name in the top-left corner; one per screen.

action.purpose: the shot button's label; the piece name in the unrolled bar.

label.purpose: edge names, panel headings, a pressed segment.

body.purpose: every other word: row labels, hints, buttons, captions on the ground.

value.purpose: setting values, seeds, take ids, sizes; a folded chip's value at 13 px.

key.purpose: the key cap beside every control that has a key.

shadows.name: glass
shadows.purpose: every glass surface and the shot; always with backdrop-filter: blur(28px) saturate(1.3).

shadows.name: flat-piece-lift
shadows.purpose: a flat piece set down on the ground.

motion.name: quiet-fade
motion.purpose: opacity and border-colour changes: a row's copy button, a take's edge, the zoom box tools.

motion.name: still-loader
motion.purpose: a toast's loader stays still; a shot shows progress as a fill growing from the left.

breakpoints.name: phone
breakpoints.purpose: the unrolled edge tabs drop their keys.

breakpoints.name: ring
breakpoints.purpose: below it the ring unrolls into a scrolling column under the art.

components.name: Glass Card
components.description: a corner card: the piece, its seed and look; every surface over the art is this glass.

components.name: Edge Chip
components.description: a folded edge on the corners' 16 px line: its group, one live value, its number key.

components.name: Shot Button

components.name: Segmented Control
components.description: day or night, the view tools, the unrolled edge tabs; the pressed segment differs in fill and weight.

components.name: Fill Button

components.name: Find Field

components.name: Setting Row
components.description: one setting on an open edge: muted label, exact mono value, a 2 px ink slider with a 3 × 14 blade.
components.html: exposure1.00
components.css: .ds-row { font-family: 'Hanken Grotesk Variable', system-ui, sans-serif; width: 268px; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 6px; } .ds-row-head { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; } .ds-row-label { font-size: 14px; color: #b9c3c9; } .ds-row-value { font-family: 'Azeret Mono Variable', ui-monospace, Menlo, monospace; font-size: 12px; color: #f2f5f7; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-track { position: relative; height: 2px; background: rgb(185 195 201 / 0.4); border-radius: 1px; margin: 6px 0; } .ds-range { position: absolute; inset: 0 60% 0 0; background: #f2f5f7; border-radius: 1px; } .ds-blade { position: absolute; left: 40%; top: -6px; width: 3px; height: 14px; background: #f2f5f7; border-radius: 1px; cursor: grab; } .ds-blade:hover { box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgb(242 245 247 / 0.25); } .ds-blade:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #f2f5f7; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Ring Switch
components.description: a toggle as an ink outline; on, it fills with ink and the knob turns dark.

narrative.overview:
The piece is the room. It is fitted whole, as large as the window allows, and everything else is smoked glass laid over its edges: dark, blurred, a little saturated, so the art reads through the controls instead of beside them. One smoke serves both themes. The theme only picks the ground a day piece sits on; a night piece always sits on the dark ground, because a pale surround reads its darks darker.

The ui is quiet and exact. Text is one grotesk at 14 px, numbers and keys are one mono at 12 px, and every control prints the key it answers to. There is exactly one loud surface on screen: the shot, opaque ink on the smoke. State is carried by shape and weight (a dashed edge, a filled segment, a word), never by a hue, and the palette has no hue to spend anyway: it is ink on smoke over the art's own colour.

Density is low by rule. Four folded edges and four corner cards are all that cover the piece at rest; one edge opens at a time.
keyCharacteristics: the piece fitted whole and biggest; all the glass shares one frame, the window's 16 px inset
one smoked glass (blur 28 px, saturate 1.3) in both themes
achromatic: ink, muted ink and ink-alpha fills; colour belongs to the art
the shot is the single opaque control
every control shows its key in a 4 px mono key cap
state by shape and weight, never by colour alone

rules.name: The One Smoke Rule
rules.body: The glass is the same smoke in light and dark. A theme changes the ground, never the glass.

rules.name: The One Loud Moment Rule
rules.body: Opaque ink fills exactly one control on screen: the shot. Everything else in the glass is ink text on smoke or an ink wash.

rules.name: The Night Ground Rule
rules.body: A night piece sits on the dark ground whatever the theme.

rules.name: The Mono Is Data Rule
rules.body: Azeret Mono holds values and keys only. A word, a label or a heading in mono is a defect.

rules.name: The Floor Rule
rules.body: Text is never below 14 px; values and keys never below 12 px. No uppercase, no tracking-wide labels.

rules.name: The Biggest Thing Rule
rules.body: At every width the piece is the largest element on screen. A panel that would shrink it overlaps it or unrolls below it instead.

rules.name: The One Frame Rule
rules.body: Every glass piece sits on one frame, the window's 16 px inset. The top and bottom pills keep the corner cards' line, so the chrome reads as one horizontal rhythm; where the art reaches the window's edge, they sit over it exactly as the corners do.

rules.name: The Blur Is The Glass Rule
rules.body: Smoke without its blur reads as grey paint; any new floating surface takes the full blur.

rules.name: The Keyboard Ring Rule
rules.body: Focus is a 2 px ink outline, offset 2 px, shown only after keyboard input. Anything that covers the art draws it inset (−4 px), because the piece reaches the window's edges.

dos: Do fit the piece whole and keep it the biggest thing on screen, at every width.
Do build every new surface over the art from the glass: `smoke`, the glass edge, the glass shadow, blur 28 px, saturate 1.3, 12 px radius.
Do print the key a control answers to, in a key cap, on the control.
Do carry state in shape, weight or words (a dashed edge, a semibold pressed segment, «current», «stashed») with any fill change.
Do keep Azeret Mono for values and keys, Hanken Grotesk for every word, in the app's lowercase voice.
Do keep loaders still; a long step shows its progress as a fill and a word, not a spin.
donts: Don't open two edges at once; the film strip is the bottom edge.
Don't signal state by colour alone.
Don't place the piece anywhere but biggest, or crop it to make room.
Don't let `/` (or any single-key command) fire inside a text field.
Don't give a second control the opaque ink of the shot.
Don't introduce a hue into the ui; colour belongs to the art.
Don't set text below 14 px or a value or key below 12 px.
Don't make the smoke differ between themes, or float glass without its blur.
